records.name: Philip Brookes Mason
records.bio: Mason was a physician, naturalist and major private collector at Burton-on-Trent. His collection included Blaschka models and later dispersed, making him important for tracing how privately assembled scientific collections entered later museum histories.

records.name: Andrew McClellan
records.bio: In 2006 McClellan rediscovered Tufts archival correspondence that pointed back to Corning custody. That documentary find reopened a collection thought to have been destroyed in the 1975 Barnum Hall fire and led to the 2007 return of ten models.

records.name: Frederick McCoy
records.bio: McCoy was a naturalist and founding museum director in Melbourne. One acquisition hypothesis links him and Henry Ward to the Melbourne Blaschka models, but the project keeps that route open until the person-level transaction evidence can be closed.
records.open: The exact transaction route by which the Melbourne collection was acquired remains unresolved.

records.name: Paul Perrot
records.bio: Perrot, a director of the Corning Museum of Glass, appears in later loan and custody histories of Blaschka collections. The project retains his record while distinguishing the general institutional role from individual object-level decisions that still require file-level confirmation.
records.open: His precise role in individual Blaschka loans and custody decisions remains to be resolved from institutional files.

records.name: Isabelle Pirotte
records.bio: Pirotte is a conservator-restorer associated with the 2008 treatment of the Geneva Blaschka collection. Her record belongs to the later material history of the models, where conservation becomes part of provenance rather than an afterthought.

records.name: Ludwig Reichenbach
records.bio: As director of Dresden’s natural-history museum and botanical garden, Reichenbach helped place Leopold’s early glass work in a scientific museum setting. His role is therefore institutional as well as personal: he belongs to the early chain through which modelling moved from private patronage toward public scientific display.

records.name: Henri Reiling
records.bio: Reiling is a modern scholar whose cataloguing and collection research has been repeatedly used to identify, compare and reconstruct surviving Blaschka holdings. His work forms part of the project’s research history and source genealogy.

records.name: Emmanuel G. Reynaud
records.bio: Reynaud is a researcher involved in reconstructing Irish Blaschka collection histories and later digital work around surviving holdings. His record marks the modern research network through which dispersed collections are being reidentified and connected.

records.name: Stuart Oliver Ridley
records.bio: Ridley was a zoologist in the British Museum’s Department of Zoology and appears in the institutional context of Blaschka collection records. The broader museum connection is secure, while the exact person-specific transaction role remains under review.
records.open: Person-specific transaction documentation for the British Museum Blaschka holdings remains incomplete.
